source_refs.note: Topic 12.5.2 with Figures 12.4 and 12.5 and Quick Check 12.2, printed pages 277-278.

blocks.text: NOₓ take part in a series of reactions leading to the formation of ozone (O₃), aldehydes, peroxyacyl nitrates (PANs) and peroxybenzoyl nitrate (PBN). PAN is one of the members of peroxyacyl nitrates as shown in Figure 12.4.

blocks.alt: Structure: R bonded to a C that carries a double-bonded O above it; the C is bonded to O, which is bonded to a second O, which is bonded to N. The N carries a + charge, a double-bonded O to the right and a single-bonded O with a minus charge below.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.4: General structure of PANs (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.4).

blocks.text: The R group in peroxyacetyl nitrate is CH₃, but other hydrocarbon chains may also be present.

The formation of PAN is illustrated in Figure 12.5. The main component of oxidizing smog is ozone, which oxidizes hydrocarbon to produce aldehyde. The aldehyde then reacts with hydroxyl radical to produce acyl radical. The acyl radical reacts with oxygen to produce peroxyacyl radical, which finally reacts with nitrogen peroxide to form peroxyacyl nitrate.

blocks.alt: A cycle drawn as an ellipse with clockwise arrows. Reactive Hydrocarbon (green box) reacts with O3 to give RCH2• at the top of the cycle; with O2 this gives RCH2O2•; with NO it gives RCH2O• + NO2; with O2 it gives HO2 + RCHO at the bottom; HO2 with NO gives NO2 + HO• on the left; HO• with RCH3 gives RCH2• again. From RCHO a vertical chain: with OH• to RC•=O, with O2 to RC(=O)OO•, with NO2 to RC(=O)OONO2.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.5: Mechanism of PAN formation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.5).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 12.5 has three slips: RCH2O. for RCH2O2., OONO3 for OONO2 in the PAN formula, and reversed arrows on the left half of the cycle. They are drawn correctly above.

blocks.prompt:
a) Draw the structures of the following oxides of nitrogen. Also, briefly explain their bonding.
i) N₂O
ii) NO
iii) NO₂
blocks.explanation:
i) N₂O is linear: N≡N–O (or N=N=O); the oxidation state of nitrogen is +1.
ii) NO has 11 valence electrons (an odd number): an N=O double bond and one unpaired electron on nitrogen, so it is paramagnetic; it weakly joins up to form the dimer N₂O₂.
iii) NO₂ is bent, O–N=O, with one unpaired electron on nitrogen (paramagnetic); two NO₂ molecules join through an N–N bond to form N₂O₄.

answer_figure.alt: Lewis structures of three nitrogen oxides: (i) N2O, linear, two resonance forms, N triple-bond N single-bond O and N=N=O, with formal charges; (ii) NO, an N=O double bond with one lone pair and one red unpaired electron on N; (iii) NO2, bent, O=N-O, angle 134 degrees, one red unpaired electron on N, + on N and - on the single-bonded O.
answer_figure.caption: Answer diagram: the structures of N₂O (linear, two resonance forms), NO (N=O, one unpaired electron) and NO₂ (bent, O=N–O, one unpaired electron).
answer_figure.long_description: The first line shows the two resonance structures of N₂O, :N≡N⁺–O⁻ and ⁻N=N⁺=O; both are linear. The second line shows NO: an N=O double bond, with one lone pair and one single (unpaired) electron (red dot) on nitrogen, 11 valence electrons in all. The third line shows NO₂: a bent molecule, O=N–O, with a bond angle of about 134°; there is one unpaired electron (red dot) on nitrogen, a + formal charge on nitrogen and a − formal charge on the single-bonded oxygen. Because of the unpaired electron, NO and NO₂ are paramagnetic.

blocks.prompt: b) What does PAN stand for? Give its general formula.
blocks.explanation: PAN stands for peroxyacyl nitrate (peroxyacetyl nitrate when R = CH₃). General formula: RC(O)OONO₂.

blocks.prompt: c) Write down the formulas of the compounds responsible for the formation of PAN.
blocks.explanation: Hydrocarbons (VOCs, for example RCH₃), ozone O₃, the hydroxyl radical HO•, oxygen O₂ and nitrogen dioxide NO₂.

blocks.prompt: d) If magnesium ribbon is ignited and placed in a jar containing N₂O, it continues to burn brightly, how does the product form in this reaction confirm the structure of N₂O?
blocks.explanation: The reaction is Mg + N₂O → MgO + N₂. When the oxygen is removed an N₂ molecule is left, which shows that in N₂O the two nitrogen atoms are bonded to each other and the oxygen is at one end: N–N–O, as shown in Table 12.2.
